The goal is to improve the user interaction with AR/VR applications, for manned and unmanned missions, such as for astronaut training, test design verification, remote testing, virtual spacecraft monitoring and control, advanced data visualization and remote support. In astronaut training and operations, during the execution of procedures in AR/VR, the selection and control of (virtual) tools, such as wrenches, pliers and cutters is essential. The use of interactive gloves is promising in this context and shall be further explored in this activity. The provision of feedback (vibrations) to indicate e.g. when contact is made, will be very helpful for the astronaut, to understand the progress and completion of performed activities. In spacecraft operations, AR/VR can be applied to remote maintenance activities of ground stations and telescopes, as well as to virtual spacecraft applications in support of mission operations. These environments require specific mobility of the users, such as hands-free operations or operations in tight spaces and also the ubiquitous use e.g. in control rooms. Here, devices that register gestures (e.g. Leap Motion) or 3D mouse devices shall be studied, in addition to the use of gloves. In testing, AR/VR can be applied to support the test execution. In addition, the mechanical design of test equipment could be supported, where the test setup can be verified more comprehensively in advanceof the actual testing. The constraints on the interaction with the AR/VR applications are very similar to the use cases for training and operations as described above.
